description: Canonical probability reasoning behavior for A.R.I.A. The Probability Engine initializes, updates, regularizes, normalizes, calibrates, preserves, and explains numerical belief across case-specific hypotheses. It consumes canonical Hypothesis, Evidence, Context, Experience, Relationship, and Confidence contracts without redefining their semantics.

core_principle.statement: Probability is a dynamic numerical representation of current belief about a hypothesis under the available evidence, context, and applicable prior information. Probability is not truth, certainty, confidence, blame, technical severity, action priority, or route priority.
rules: Probability values shall remain within the inclusive range 0.0 through 1.0.
Probability shall remain distinct from confidence.
Historical information may influence priors but is not current-case evidence.
Current applicable evidence may update prior belief.
Strong applicable current evidence may overcome strong historical priors.
Small or weak historical samples shall not create unsupported extreme priors.
Dependent evidence shall not be multiplied as though independent.
Unknown probability shall be preserved when the modeled hypothesis set may be incomplete.
Mutually exclusive and coexisting hypotheses shall not be treated identically.
Hierarchical hypotheses shall not be double counted.
Probability changes shall remain explainable and historically reconstructable.
Probability Engine shall not independently confirm or eliminate hypotheses.
The Probability Engine shall remain technically domain-independent.
Probability Engine shall not define a competing hypothesis_probability_record.
Probability state shall be persisted through the canonical Hypothesis Schema.
Probability Engine may propose updates to probability-owned fields without owning the complete Hypothesis record.
Probability history shall conform to hypothesis.schema.json.
Probability Engine shall not create a second probability persistence object unless a future canonical schema explicitly establishes one.
Hypothesis Engine remains authoritative for hypothesis reasoning state and status transitions.

confidence_boundary.principle: Probability confidence describes confidence in the quality and calibration of a probability estimate and shall never be interpreted as the probability itself.
rules: Probability Engine shall consume the canonical confidence contract.
Probability Engine shall not define competing qualitative confidence levels.
Probability confidence shall reflect uncertainty in the probability estimate.
A hypothesis may have high probability with low probability confidence.
A hypothesis may have moderate probability with high probability confidence.
Confidence shall not be used as a substitute for probability.
Probability shall not be used as a substitute for confidence.
Unknown confidence shall remain unknown rather than being assigned an invented numeric value.
Confidence precision shall not exceed the quality of the underlying basis.

MUTUALLY_EXCLUSIVE.description: A defined hypothesis group in which only one member may explain the modeled condition under the applicable technical model.

COEXISTING.description: Hypotheses representing conditions that may simultaneously be true.

HIERARCHICAL.description: Hypotheses representing different levels or branches of specificity within a causal hierarchy.

UNKNOWN_RELATIONSHIP.description: Hypotheses for which exclusivity, coexistence, or hierarchical dependency has not yet been sufficiently established.

probability_pipeline.name: RECEIVE_HYPOTHESIS_SET
probability_pipeline.description: Receive canonical case-specific hyp_<UUID> records requiring probability initialization or recalculation.

probability_pipeline.name: RESOLVE_PROBABILITY_STRUCTURE
probability_pipeline.description: Determine whether relevant hypotheses are mutually exclusive, coexisting, hierarchical, dependent, or insufficiently characterized.

probability_pipeline.name: RETRIEVE_APPLICABLE_PRIOR_INFORMATION
probability_pipeline.description: Retrieve validated historical information and applicable prior components without treating historical information as current-case evidence.

probability_pipeline.name: ASSESS_PRIOR_APPLICABILITY
probability_pipeline.description: Consume canonical Context and Experience assessments to determine how strongly historical populations apply.

probability_pipeline.name: REGULARIZE_PRIORS
probability_pipeline.description: Apply Bayesian or equivalent shrinkage so sparse or weak historical samples do not create unsupported extreme priors.

probability_pipeline.name: INITIALIZE_PROBABILITY
probability_pipeline.description: Calculate initial probability and probability confidence for newly active hypotheses.

probability_pipeline.name: RETRIEVE_APPLICABLE_EVIDENCE_EFFECTS
probability_pipeline.description: Consume Evidence assessments, canonical relationships, quality, applicability, independence, and contradiction information relevant to each hypothesis.

probability_pipeline.name: CALCULATE_EVIDENCE_UPDATES
probability_pipeline.description: Update belief using calibrated likelihood treatment or another explicitly identified probability method.

probability_pipeline.name: CONTROL_DEPENDENCY
probability_pipeline.description: Prevent duplicated or dependent evidence from producing artificial probability amplification.

probability_pipeline.name: NORMALIZE_WHERE_REQUIRED
probability_pipeline.description: Normalize only within valid mutually exclusive probability groups while preserving unknown probability when the group is not exhaustive.

probability_pipeline.name: ASSESS_PROBABILITY_CONFIDENCE
probability_pipeline.description: Assess confidence in the resulting probability estimate using the canonical confidence architecture.

probability_pipeline.name: APPLY_CERTAINTY_GUARDS
probability_pipeline.description: Prevent unsupported mathematical certainty and preserve explicit deterministic exceptions.

probability_pipeline.name: GENERATE_PROBABILITY_HISTORY
probability_pipeline.description: Record material probability changes, their basis, method, and applicable evidence or prior influences.

probability_pipeline.name: RETURN_PROBABILITY_RESULT
probability_pipeline.description: Return probability updates and material changes to Orchestration for Hypothesis, Uncertainty, Decision, Validation, and Case State coordination.

prior_model.principle: Priors represent belief before incorporating the current update set and shall be based only on sufficiently applicable and eligible historical information.
rules: Canonical prior components shall conform to hypothesis.schema.json.
Probability Engine shall not invent additional persisted prior fields outside the schema.
Not every prior component is required for every hypothesis.
Unavailable prior components shall remain unavailable rather than being fabricated.
More specific prior information shall not automatically override broader prior information.
Specific historical populations require sufficient applicable support before receiving substantial influence.
Sparse specific populations shall shrink toward broader applicable populations.
Historical information excluded from learning shall not silently influence learned priors.
Historical frequency shall never be represented as current-case evidence.
Prior construction shall preserve provenance and method.
Probability Engine may calculate statistical influence from canonical assessments supplied by other engines.
Probability Engine shall not recreate Evidence quality semantics.
Probability Engine shall not recreate Context dimension semantics.
Probability Engine shall not independently declare historical cases eligible for learning.
Missing applicability information shall reduce confidence rather than be assumed favorable.

hierarchical_prior_model.principle: Broad and specific historical populations may be combined using hierarchical shrinkage so specificity increases influence only when supported by sufficient applicable data.
rules: Conceptual specificity does not imply automatic precedence.
A broad population may outweigh a highly specific population when the specific sample is weak.
A strong sufficiently sized specific population may increasingly dominate broader populations.
Context applicability and effective sample size shall influence prior weighting.
The combined prior shall preserve the method used.
Prior construction shall avoid double counting historical cases appearing in multiple overlapping populations.
Nested historical populations shall be modeled as hierarchical information rather than independent evidence.
Regularization shall prevent small samples from producing unsupported certainty.
Regularization strength may decrease as sufficiently validated effective sample size increases.
Hyperparameters shall remain traceable to their basis.
Raw historical rates shall remain available for audit when calculated.
The selected method shall be recorded in the persisted prior or probability history where applicable.
A.R.I.A. shall not claim Bayesian precision when the required data is unavailable.
Raw sample size and effective sample size shall remain distinguishable.
Duplicate historical records shall not inflate effective sample size.
Dependent historical records shall receive reduced independent influence.
Low-learning-confidence experience shall contribute less than strongly validated experience.
Poorly applicable historical cases shall contribute less than strongly applicable cases.
Effective sample size shall not exceed what the underlying independent information reasonably supports.

context_boundary.principle: Probability consumes context applicability; it does not own the universal Context model.
rules: Context Engine owns context dimensions and context resolution.
Probability Engine may consume context-match values, applicable context references, and material context differences.
Probability Engine shall not hardcode manufacturer, product, firmware, topology, environment, user, or other dimensions as a competing universal Context contract.
The importance of context differences may vary by hypothesis.
Missing context shall reduce probability confidence when materially relevant.
Material context changes may require prior and posterior recalculation.

experience_boundary.principle: Validated Experience may influence priors only to the extent permitted by learning eligibility, applicability, and confidence.
rules: Experience is not current-case evidence.
Probability Engine shall not create Experience records.
Probability Engine shall not determine learning eligibility.
Experience excluded from statistical learning shall not silently contribute to empirical priors.
Experience may contribute differently to different hypotheses depending on applicability.
Historical attribution shall not be converted into blame.
User-specific or team-specific history shall be used only when technically relevant and statistically defensible.
Protected, sensitive, or irrelevant personal characteristics shall never influence technical probability.

recency_model.principle: Historical predictive influence may change with time when the underlying technical population, process, product, competency, or environment changes.
rules: Recency modifies predictive influence, not historical truth.
Stable technical facts shall not decay merely because they are old.
Decay shall be applied only when time plausibly changes predictive applicability.
Revision-aware applicability may be more appropriate than simple time decay.
Decay parameters shall remain configurable and explainable.
Recency shall not silently erase historical records.

evidence_boundary.principle: Evidence Engine determines what evidence represents and assesses its quality, applicability, provenance, verification, independence, and diagnostic effect; Probability Engine determines how applicable evidence changes numerical belief.
rules: Probability Engine shall consume canonical evd_<UUID> references and applicable relationship semantics.
Probability Engine shall not recreate Evidence records.
Probability Engine shall not independently reclassify evidence type.
Probability Engine shall not independently override Evidence dependency assessments without an explicit reasoning conflict being surfaced.
Evidence confidence and hypothesis probability shall remain distinct.
Contradictory evidence shall not be discarded because it conflicts with the leading hypothesis.
Evidence updates shall remain attributable to the evidence that caused them.
Likelihood values shall preserve provenance or calibration basis.
A.R.I.A. shall not invent precise likelihood ratios when insufficient information exists.
Empirically learned likelihoods shall be used only when learning eligibility and calibration support them.
Qualitative evidence effects may be converted into conservative probability updates when empirical likelihoods are unavailable.
The selected update method shall remain explainable.
Evidence updates shall not exceed what evidence quality and applicability reasonably support.

qualitative_update_policy.principle: When quantitative likelihood data is unavailable, qualitative evidence effects may produce conservative bounded updates without pretending that arbitrary constants are universal physical laws.
rules: Qualitative effect classes shall align with Evidence Engine semantics.
Generic fixed likelihood-ratio ranges shall not be treated as canonical universal constants.
Implementation calibration may define bounded mappings outside the universal reasoning contract.
Weak or uncertain evidence shall produce conservative movement.
EFFECT_UNKNOWN shall not produce an invented directional update.
NO_MATERIAL_EFFECT shall not materially move probability.
CONTEXTUALIZES may alter applicability or confidence without directly changing probability.

evidence_quality_modulation.principle: Evidence update strength shall be moderated by the quality and applicability of the evidence without conflating those factors with hypothesis probability.
evidence_quality_modulation.conceptual_method: Shrink an evidence update toward neutral as confidence in the update basis decreases.
rules: update_reliability is a probability-calculation factor derived from applicable canonical confidence assessments and shall not create a new persisted confidence dimension.
High-quality applicable evidence may preserve more of the raw likelihood effect.
Low-quality or poorly applicable evidence shall move probability less strongly.
Unknown quality shall not be assumed equivalent to perfect quality.
Evidence confidence values shall not be interpreted as probability that the evidence is true.
The modulation method shall remain auditable.

dependent_evidence_handling.principle: Evidence sharing an underlying information source shall not receive the full multiplicative treatment appropriate to independent evidence.
rules: Evidence dependency assessments shall originate from Evidence reasoning and canonical relationships.
Duplicate representations shall not multiply probability.
Derived evidence shall not independently multiply the effect of its parents.
Partially dependent evidence may provide limited additional information.
Independent corroboration may legitimately increase probability movement.
When dependency cannot be quantified reliably, Probability Engine shall use conservative treatment.
Normalization shall occur only within a technically valid mutually exclusive probability group.
The group shall not be assumed exhaustive without sufficient technical basis.
Unknown or Other shall preserve probability mass when known hypotheses are not exhaustive.
Parent and child hypotheses representing the same causal branch shall not compete as independent peers.
Eliminated hypotheses may be excluded from active normalization when elimination is technically established.
Normalization shall not convert weak evidence into strong confidence.
The normalization group and method shall remain explainable.

coexisting_probability_handling.principle: Hypotheses capable of simultaneously being true shall maintain probability estimates that are not constrained to sum to one.
rules: Coexisting hypothesis probabilities are not required to sum to 1.0.
Confirmation of one coexisting condition shall not automatically reduce unrelated coexisting probability.
Known dependency between coexisting hypotheses shall be modeled rather than ignored.
Conditional probabilities may be used where one condition changes the likelihood of another.
Probability Engine shall not force coexistence into mutual exclusivity for computational convenience.

hierarchical_probability_handling.principle: Probabilities within a causal hierarchy shall preserve parent-child dependency and avoid double counting the same underlying explanation.
rules: A child probability may be conditional on its parent branch.
Sibling hypotheses may form a normalized mutually exclusive set beneath a parent when technically appropriate.
Child probabilities shall not independently add to the parent as though unrelated.
Probability mass may be refined from a broad branch into more specific children as evidence discriminates the branch.
Hypothesis Engine owns whether a broader hypothesis becomes SUPERSEDED.
Probability Engine shall preserve the probability logic used during refinement.

unknown_probability.principle: Unknown probability represents belief assigned to explanations not adequately represented by the currently modeled known hypothesis set.
rules: Unknown probability shall be preserved when the known mutually exclusive hypothesis group may be incomplete.
Unknown probability may increase when known hypotheses are repeatedly weakened without an adequate alternative.
Unknown probability may decrease when evidence supports a sufficiently comprehensive known explanation set.
Unknown probability shall not be forced to zero merely because one known hypothesis leads.
Unknown probability shall not be used as a dumping ground for numerical rounding error.
Persistent material unknown probability shall be surfaced to Orchestration.
Hypothesis Engine owns generation of additional known or unknown hypotheses.

certainty_guards.principle: Mathematical certainty shall require stronger justification than ordinary probabilistic preference.
rules: Guardrails are implementation defaults rather than universal technical constants.
Probability exactly 0.0 should normally require deterministic incompatibility or sufficiently validated exclusion.
Probability exactly 1.0 should normally require deterministic implication or sufficiently validated confirmation basis.
Hypothesis status remains owned by Hypothesis Engine.
Guardrails shall not override explicit deterministic technical rules.
Guardrails may be calibrated based on validated system behavior.

probability_confidence_model.principle: Probability confidence expresses how well supported, calibrated, applicable, and stable the probability estimate itself is.
rules: Probability confidence shall use the canonical confidence contract.
Probability confidence shall not be calculated merely from the magnitude of current_probability.
Extreme probability with weak basis may have low confidence.
Stable probability under multiple reasonable assumptions may justify greater confidence.
High unknown probability may reduce confidence in individual known-hypothesis probabilities.
Unresolved evidence dependency may reduce probability confidence.
Insufficient calibration data shall reduce confidence in numerically precise updates.
Probability confidence shall remain explainable.

sensitivity_analysis.principle: When probability materially depends on uncertain assumptions, A.R.I.A. should assess whether reasonable changes to those assumptions would change the diagnostic ranking or decision relevance.
rules: Sensitivity analysis is most important when a decision materially depends on close probability differences.
A result highly sensitive to weak assumptions shall receive lower probability confidence.
Sensitivity analysis shall not manufacture precision.
Material rank instability shall be surfaced to Uncertainty and Decision through Orchestration.

calibration.principle: Probability estimates should become empirically calibrated over time using sufficiently validated, learning-eligible outcomes.
rules: Calibration shall use learning-eligible validated outcomes.
Cases excluded from learning shall not silently influence calibration.
Calibration shall compare predicted probability with validated outcomes rather than subjective retrospective confidence.
Calibration may be global or context-specific when sufficient sample support exists.
Small calibration samples shall not justify aggressive model correction.
Calibration changes shall remain versioned and auditable.
Probability Engine shall not redefine learning eligibility.

probability_history.principle: Material probability changes shall remain reconstructable.
record_when: material evidence is invalidated or retracted
rules: Probability history shall conform to hypothesis.schema.json.
Historical probability entries shall not be rewritten using later knowledge.
Each material update shall preserve its calculation method and basis.
Applicable evidence references shall be preserved.
Prior changes and evidence-driven changes shall remain distinguishable.
Probability history shall support reconstruction of what A.R.I.A. believed at the time.

recalculation_rules: Probability shall be recalculated when a material input to the previous calculation changes.
Recalculation shall preserve prior probability history.
Invalidated or retracted evidence shall no longer contribute as active probability support.
Superseded evidence shall be treated according to current applicability rather than deleted from history.
A changed hypothesis group may require renormalization.
A material context change may require both prior and evidence applicability reevaluation.
Recalculation shall not silently alter historical entries.

hypothesis_boundary.principle: Probability Engine calculates numerical belief; Hypothesis Engine owns hypothesis semantics and state.
rules: Probability Engine shall not generate canonical hypotheses.
Probability Engine shall not directly set CANDIDATE, ACTIVE, DEPRIORITIZED, UNLIKELY, ELIMINATED, CONFIRMED, or SUPERSEDED status.
Probability Engine may report probability conditions relevant to Hypothesis state reevaluation.
Low probability alone shall not eliminate a hypothesis.
High probability alone shall not confirm a hypothesis.
Probability Engine shall respect coexistence and hierarchy supplied by Hypothesis and canonical relationships.
Material probability changes shall be returned to Orchestration.

uncertainty_boundary.principle: Probability quantifies belief among hypotheses; Uncertainty Engine reasons about what remains unknown, unresolved, incomplete, ambiguous, or insufficiently discriminated.
rules: Probability Engine shall not redefine uncertainty state.
Unknown probability may be an input to uncertainty reasoning.
Low probability confidence may be an input to uncertainty reasoning.
Sensitivity and calibration limitations may be surfaced to Uncertainty.
A normalized probability distribution does not imply low uncertainty.
A leading hypothesis does not imply adequate diagnostic certainty.

decision_boundary.principle: Probability informs Decision but does not select Actions.
rules: Decision Engine may consume current_probability and probability_confidence.
Probability Engine shall not choose act_<UUID>.
Highest probability does not automatically imply the corresponding corrective Action should be selected.
Decision may consider probability together with information value, consequence, cost, burden, reversibility, service impact, and risk.
Probability Engine shall not convert probability directly into route priority.

routing_boundary.principle: Probability does not own operational progression.
rules: Probability Engine shall not create route steps.
Probability Engine shall not select next hops.
Probability Engine shall not reroute.
Probability changes may cause Decision reevaluation through Orchestration.
Routing Engine remains responsible for route progression after Action selection.

validation_boundary.principle: Validation results may materially update probability, but Probability Engine does not define validation success.
rules: Validation Engine owns validation semantics.
Validation-generated evidence may update hypothesis probability.
Successful validation may strongly support a hypothesis when causally discriminating.
Symptom improvement alone shall not automatically produce probability 1.0.
Failed validation may reduce a hypothesis probability or increase alternatives and unknown probability.
Probability changes from validation shall remain attributable to resulting evidence and relationships.

case_state_boundary.principle: Case State projects current probability information but does not calculate it.
rules: Probability Engine owns probability calculation.
Case State may project current_probability and probability_confidence from canonical Hypothesis records.
Probability Engine shall not change case lifecycle status.
Probability Engine shall not change case reasoning state.
Probability alone shall not resolve or close a case.

orchestration_boundary.principle: Probability Engine returns probability reasoning results; Orchestration coordinates downstream effects.
rules: Probability Engine shall not directly invoke every downstream engine.
Material probability changes shall be returned to Orchestration.
Orchestration determines whether Hypothesis, Uncertainty, Decision, Routing, Validation, or Case State require reevaluation.
Probability Engine shall not publish complete Case State.
Probability recalculation may be invoked repeatedly as evidence, context, hypothesis structure, or learning state changes.
Outputs shall distinguish persisted fields from calculation metadata.
Outputs shall not change Hypothesis status directly.
Outputs shall not fabricate precision unsupported by the calculation basis.
Outputs shall preserve uncertainty.
Outputs shall not select Actions.
Material changes shall be returned to Orchestration.

required_questions: What prior information influenced the calculation?
What current evidence changed the probability?
How confident is A.R.I.A. in the probability estimate?
What assumptions materially influence the result?
rules: Probability explanations shall distinguish historical prior influence from current evidence influence.
Probability explanations shall not imply certainty when probability confidence is limited.
Probability explanations shall identify major assumptions and limitations.
Human-readable explanations shall remain consistent with persisted calculation history.

failure_modes.description: Probability Engine creates a competing persisted hypothesis probability record.
Probability and confidence are treated as the same quantity.
failure_modes.prevention: Use current_probability separately from canonical probability_confidence.

failure_modes.description: Probability Engine defines competing confidence levels or semantics.
Probability Engine hardcodes a competing universal context model.
Probability Engine independently redefines evidence quality, provenance, or dependency.
Historical cases are treated as current-case observations.
failure_modes.prevention: Use historical information only through priors and calibration.

failure_modes.description: Sparse historical observations create extreme priors.
failure_modes.prevention: Use hierarchical Bayesian regularization and effective sample size.

failure_modes.description: Dependent or duplicate evidence is multiplied as though independent.
Known hypotheses are normalized to 1.0 despite an incomplete candidate set.
Coexisting hypotheses are incorrectly normalized to sum to one.
Parent and child hypotheses are treated as independent competing causes.
A.R.I.A. invents precise likelihood ratios without empirical or calibrated basis.
failure_modes.prevention: Use conservative qualitative updates and preserve calibration limitations.

failure_modes.description: High probability directly confirms a hypothesis.
Low probability directly eliminates a hypothesis.
Highest probability automatically determines the selected Action.
Probability Engine directly changes route progression.
Historical outcomes influence future probability without sufficient validation or learning eligibility.
failure_modes.prevention: Use only learning-eligible validated historical information.

failure_modes.description: User-specific historical probability is interpreted as blame or universal fault propensity.
failure_modes.prevention: Use only technically relevant, contextual, statistically defensible historical information.

failure_modes.description: Universal Probability Engine logic hardcodes specific technologies, vendors, products, customers, organizations, or named users.

invariants.statement: Probability values remain within the inclusive range 0.0 through 1.0.
Probability and confidence remain distinct.
Probability persistence is owned by Core/Schemas/hypothesis.schema.json.
Confidence vocabulary is owned by Core/Registries/confidence_levels.json.
Historical information influences priors but is not current-case evidence.
Sparse historical samples do not create unsupported certainty.
Dependent evidence is not multiplied as though independent.
Mutually exclusive hypotheses are normalized only within technically valid probability groups.
Coexisting hypothesis probabilities are not required to sum to one.
Hierarchical hypotheses are not double counted.
Unknown probability is preserved when the modeled hypothesis set may be incomplete.
Probability Engine does not independently confirm hypotheses.
Probability Engine does not independently eliminate hypotheses.
Probability Engine consumes rather than recreates Evidence quality and dependency semantics.
Probability Engine consumes rather than recreates Context semantics.
Probability Engine does not determine learning eligibility.
Probability Engine does not select competitive Actions.
Probability Engine does not perform route progression or rerouting.
Material probability changes remain historically reconstructable.
Probability Engine remains technically domain-independent.

prohibited_behaviors: Defining a competing hypothesis probability persistence record.
Defining competing confidence levels or confidence semantics.
Treating probability as confidence.
Treating confidence as probability.
Treating probability as truth or certainty.
Treating historical experience as current-case evidence.
Using learning-ineligible historical cases in learned priors without explicit authorization.
Allowing sparse samples to create unsupported extreme priors.
Treating more specific historical populations as automatically superior to broader populations.
Double counting overlapping historical populations.
Hardcoding a competing Context dimension vocabulary.
Recreating Evidence quality, provenance, verification, or dependency semantics.
Multiplying duplicate or dependent evidence as though independent.
Inventing precise likelihood ratios without sufficient basis.
Treating generic qualitative likelihood mappings as immutable technical constants.
Normalizing coexisting hypotheses to sum to one.
Normalizing an incomplete known hypothesis set without preserving unknown probability.
Treating parent and child hypotheses as independent competing causes.
Forcing unknown probability to zero because a known hypothesis leads.
Setting a hypothesis to CONFIRMED solely because probability is high.
Setting a hypothesis to ELIMINATED solely because probability is low.
Directly selecting act_<UUID>.
Directly creating route steps.
Directly rerouting.
Directly changing case lifecycle status.
Directly changing case reasoning state.
Using user-specific historical patterns as blame.
Using irrelevant or protected personal characteristics to influence technical probability.
Directly invoking downstream engines as a substitute for Orchestration.
Rewriting historical probability entries using later knowledge.

Hardcoding microwave-specific, RF-specific, optical-specific, vendor-specific, manufacturer-specific, product-specific, protocol-specific, customer-specific, organization-specific, or named-user probability logic into the universal Probability Engine.
